Elaine (Sales): quick heads-up — LexaAPI POC kickoff this week. Customer is asking if we can match their current responses exactly enough for a drop-in migration (they use a shim today). Need plan for mapping surface area + any enterprise blockers :eyes:
Sam (Eng): ok. main risks are: different tokenizers -> token counts, response shape (Lexa returns `data.items[]` vs our `choices[]`), and their post-processing hooks. we can shim but need tests for parity and perf impact.
Marta (PSE): for the POC they want 2 endpoints: text-generation (chat) and embeddings. also asking about pricing delta when using our quantized models vs their hosted ones. can we provide a rough t-shirt estimate for 100M tokens/month? :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Sam (Eng): quick estimate: with our recommended batching and prefix KV cache, unit cost should be ~30-40% lower than their standard instance. i'll give numbers after i run a couple of perf runs.
Liam (Security): security Qs from their GRC: data residency, KMS integration, audit logs retention, and SOC2 evidence. Also they asked about chaining webhooks to third-party analytics — we need to confirm we don't persist PII in logs by default.
Marta (PSE): noted. Elaine, can you share their SOC/ISO checklist? i'll prep the answers.
Elaine (Sales): shared the checklist in the customer portal link (internal only) — @Marta @Liam please review before EOD Friday so we can push the questionnaire.
Sam (Eng): for the shim we can do a lightweight adapter that:
- maps Lexa `data.items[*].text` -> `choices[*].text`
- rewrites streaming frames to our SSE format
- normalizes `usage` fields (tokens) by running their text through our tokenizer for billing parity
Example adapter snippet (pseudo):
```
POST /proxy
body -> requestMap(body) // map params
res = callRedwood(model, mapped)
return mapResponse(res) // map choices, usage
```
This will add ~30-50ms p99 on top of our baseline depending on tokenizer cost.
Marta (PSE): can we include a config toggle so the adapter can operate in a "parity mode" (more expensive but exact shape) vs "normalized mode" (cheaper, our shape)? Customer asked for both options.
Sam (Eng): yes. parity mode preserves their fields and extra metadata. normalized mode returns our canonical shape. both behind a feature flag and tested via the eval suite.
Marta (PSE): i'll prepare a short checklist for the POC: 1) mapping adapter + test vectors, 2) perf run (1000 concurrent requests), 3) tokenization parity test, 4) security questionnaire answers, 5) pricing delta memo.
Elaine (Sales): perfect. also they raised an enterprise blocker: procurement wants a clause about incident notifications and a 24h SLA for PII incidents. procurement asked if we can add that to SOW.
Liam (Security): we can commit to incident notification timelines but need legal to scope SLA language. i'll loop in Legal.
CI-bot: build 0a3b9 passed: adapter-prototype deployed to staging -> https://staging.redwood/ops/0a3b9
Sam (Eng): deployed prototype ready for smoke tests. I'll run tokenizer parity tests tomorrow morning and post results.
Marta (PSE): i'll run initial mapping tests today and send sample diffs. Elaine — can you get procurement contact so we can triage the SLA ask?
Elaine (Sales): pinged procurement and added them to the thread. next sync Friday 10am PT. :calendar: Thanks everyone.
